Lens is an open-source control plane for deploying and operating large language
models on [llm-d](https://llm-d.ai/), the Kubernetes-native distributed
inference stack, across your Kubernetes clusters. It plans and executes
inference deployments, runs guided evaluations and traffic simulations, and
keeps clusters, storage and external providers under one roof — so a team can
go from a registered model to a benchmarked, production-serving deployment
without stitching together separate tools.

<img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="Lens clusters dashboard" width="100%" />

## Highlights

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Optimal performance" icon="bolt-lightning">
    Deployments run on llm-d: prefill/decode disaggregation, KV-cache-aware
    routing, KV cache offloading to CPU/SSD tiers, and latency-predicted
    routing raise throughput and cut tail latency on the same GPUs.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Multi-cluster deployment" icon="server">
    Plan, approve and execute inference deployments across Kubernetes clusters
    from a single UI, with agentic, workload-guided placement.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Guided evaluation" icon="chart-line">
    Design benchmark experiments, run them against live deployments, and
    analyze and export the results without hand-written scripts.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Traffic simulation" icon="flask">
    Replay registered request traces against an inference endpoint to validate
    behavior and capacity before real traffic arrives.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Model Service gateway" icon="route">
    Publish cluster deployments as OpenAI-compatible model services behind the
    cluster's shared Gateway (HTTPRoute → InferencePool → EPP), with per-model
    selection policies.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Governance built in" icon="shield-check">
    Role-based access control, per-cluster scoping and audit logging apply
    across every page, from clusters to model services.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Observability" icon="gauge-high">
    Bootstrap and maintain the cluster monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana) to
    watch GPU utilization and deployment health.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Architecture

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Lens system architecture" width="100%" />

A single Lens server manages any number of Kubernetes clusters, on-premises or
in the cloud, from one pane of glass: the console talks to an application layer
over same-origin API routes, and that layer forwards requests to a control plane
that owns the domain services, persists state to the database, and drives
clusters, storage and the model-service data plane directly. Access control and
audit logging are enforced in the control plane, so every page — deployments,
evaluation, simulation and model services alike — respects the same per-cluster
permissions.
